document: قرار مجلس الوزراء رقم (1) لسنة 2022 في شأن اللائحة التنفيذية للمرسوم بقانون اتحادي رقم (33) لسنة 2021 بشأن تنظيم علاقات العمل.pdf

symptoms.tree_quality: completely flat, all nodes direct children of root

root_cause: The document is a SCANNED Arabic Cabinet Resolution (zero native text layer). Docling must OCR the page images to extract text, which produces only 294 chars total of thin/noisy output. The _inject_arabic_structural_headings() function (converters.py:135) has no meaningful Arabic text to scan for structural markers (باب/فصل/مادة/قسم/جزء). Without detected structural markers, no headings are promoted, and md_to_tree() receives a markdown with zero # headings. The pageindex library's md_to_tree then creates a flat tree with all 308 content blocks as direct children of the root node (depth=1), each block being a single line of thin OCR text.
distinguishing_factor: Unlike other RC-2 docs (e.g. cabinet_resolution_no_21_of_2020, Haftpflicht-Allgemeine-Bedingungen) which have native text layers with actual Arabic/German structural markers, this document's OCR-only path starves the heading-promotion pipeline. The E2E_CORPUS_REPORT explicitly flags this as 'Scanned Arabic Cabinet Resolution. Zero text.' with 21 image blocks and 294 total chars (vs 20k-100k chars in documents with native text). Runs 16-19 all show depth=1/308 nodes, confirming the OCR limitation is consistent, not a regression.

problem_doc.name: قرار مجلس الوزراء رقم (1) لسنة 2022 ... .pdf
problem_doc.reason_for_depth_1: OCR produces thin output with no structural markers at line starts; all 308 nodes are root children

architectural_gap.description: The heading-depth recovery chain assumes sufficient text content exists in the extracted markdown to contain recognizable numbering/structural patterns. For scanned documents with thin OCR output, this assumption fails.
architectural_gap.affected_step: All three depth-recovery steps (_relevel_by_containment, _relevel_by_numbering, _relevel_by_outline) require EITHER native headings from Docling OR enough body text to infer structure from numbering/outlines. Thin OCR provides neither.
architectural_gap.why_this_is_rc2_not_new_regression: RC-2 root cause states: 'Docling produces either all headings at same level OR no headings at all for Arabic docs'. This doc exemplifies the 'no headings' case, but specifically because OCR-only extraction produces insufficient text content, not because of a logic bug in _inject_arabic_structural_headings itself.

verification_evidence.run_16_to_19_persistence: Stalls section (line 102 of audit) confirms depth=1/308 flat blocks stable across Run 16, 18, 19 — no regression, stable limitation
verification_evidence.char_density: 294 chars / 21 image blocks ≈ 14 chars/block average, vs 1000-5000 chars/block in native-text docs, confirming sparse OCR output

suggested_fix.immediate: Acknowledge this document's OCR limitation and mark it as expected MARGINAL. The flat tree is not a code bug but a consequence of thin OCR input.
suggested_fix.medium_term: Implement TL-1 (cluster-level root cause) OCR escalation for scanned documents: detect when OCR output falls below a char-density floor (e.g. <500 chars total for a 5+ page doc) and attempt a higher-fidelity OCR path (cloud API with Arabic specialization, or multi-pass Tesseract PSM modes).
suggested_fix.validation: Before committing any heading-detection fix, measure the actual Docling markdown output for this doc by enabling debug logging of post_md/raw_md at line 3217-3218 in pdf_to_markdown_docling, confirming zero headings are actually produced.
